tech_stack: .NET 8, ASP.NET Core, SQL Server + Dapper (raw SqlDataReader + Dapper.Contrib), Kafka (Avro via Seismic.Platform.SharedEventBus.Client), Redis (LaunchDarkly), New Relic

http_deps: UserManagementService — actor identity and permission lookup
background_services: ExpirationBackgroundService — RLPolling loop that expires content versions on schedule
CustomPropertyBackgroundService — processes deferred custom property update jobs
SystemStateBackgroundService — validates and reconciles content system state
ScheduleActivateBackgroundService — activates content on scheduled datetime
ScheduleAddToProfileBackgroundService — adds content to publish profiles on schedule
SyncIndicatorBGService — updates external sync status indicators

domains.name: File
domains.responsibility: Manages content file lifecycle including creation, versioning, checkout, and soft deletion within a team site
domains.health_reason: FileManager is a pure delegation wrapper over FileRepository with no invariant-enforcing methods; checkout state transitions (IsCheckedOut, CheckedOutBy) and delete guards are mutated directly from FileWriter and Orchestrator checkpoint lambdas outside the entity

invariants: A file cannot be checked out if already checked out by another user
A file cannot be deleted while it is checked out
A file cannot be updated if the actor lacks write permission on the parent team site

domains.name: FileVersion
domains.responsibility: Tracks the version history and expiration lifecycle of content file versions
domains.health_reason: FileVersionManager is a thin wrapper around FileVersionRepository; expiration logic (QueryExpiredVersions, MarkAsExpired, RemovePublishedVersion, LogExpiration) is scattered across ExpirationJobExecutor and ExpirationBackgroundService rather than inside the entity

invariants: A version cannot be expired if it is the only active version for its content item
A version past its ExpirationDate must be marked expired before being removed from publish profiles

domains.name: Folder
domains.responsibility: Manages the hierarchical folder structure and materialized path resolution within a team site
domains.health_reason: All path materialization and hierarchy invariants are encoded in SQL queries inside FolderRepository; cycle prevention and path uniqueness rules are absent from any entity class

invariants: A folder cannot be deleted if it contains non-deleted content items
A folder path must be unique within its parent scope

domains.name: Publish
domains.responsibility: Controls the mapping of file versions to publishing profiles and tracks the publish state per profile
domains.health_reason: PublishWriter and PublishExecutor contain all publish-state validation and transition logic; PublishRepository is a pure data accessor; no aggregate enforces publish invariants — publishability checks live in IPublishOrchestrator.RequestPublishFileCheckpoint() lambda

invariants: A file version must be non-expired to be published
A file cannot be published to a profile if the actor lacks the required permission
A scheduled publish datetime must be in the future

domains.name: CustomProperty
domains.responsibility: Defines and manages custom metadata schema (definitions) and per-content property values
domains.health_reason: CustomPropertyManager uses XmlResolver and DefinitionResolver helpers that contain real schema logic; however, property value validation occurs in the application layer and the deferred-update background service runs outside domain boundaries

invariants: A custom property value must conform to its definition schema type
A required custom property cannot be left empty on content creation

domains.name: Permission
domains.responsibility: Evaluates and enforces content-level and team-site-level access control with per-request caching
domains.health_reason: ContentPermissionManager has real permission-evaluation logic and a cart-based cache, but the enforcement entry point is a checkpoint lambda in IPermissionOrchestrator rather than a method on the Permission aggregate; unique-permission limit guard lives in the orchestrator

invariants: Permission cannot be granted by an actor who does not themselves hold manage-permission rights
Unique permission count per content item cannot exceed the system limit

domains.name: ExternalSync
domains.responsibility: Manages synchronization of content items with external storage providers such as Google Drive
domains.health_reason: ExternalSyncManager and GoogleDriveManager hold the sync state machine and credential-validation logic that belongs on an ExternalSyncEntity aggregate; sync error states are tracked via raw status strings rather than lifecycle state

invariants: A sync task cannot start if the sync config is disabled
Invalid credentials must be surfaced as a domain error before any sync is attempted

domains.name: Activity
domains.responsibility: Records an immutable audit trail of all content operations for compliance and analytics
domains.health_reason: ActivityRepository.LogActivity is called imperatively from orchestrators, executors, and background services as an afterthought side-effect rather than being triggered naturally by domain events raised on aggregates; there is no DomainEvent mechanism that would make audit recording automatic

invariants: Activity records are immutable once written

domains.name: Comment
domains.responsibility: Manages user comments and page-level annotations attached to content items
domains.health_reason: CommentReader and CommentWriter delegate directly to their repositories with no business logic in entities; deletion guard (only author or admin may delete) is not encoded in the entity

invariants: A comment cannot be deleted by a user who is neither its author nor a site admin

domains.name: TeamSite
domains.responsibility: Manages team site membership, storage quota, and site-level configuration
domains.health_reason: TeamSiteMemberManager has some membership validation but quota enforcement and site configuration invariants live in the ITeamSiteOrchestrator checkpoint layer, not in the entity

invariants: A team site cannot exceed its storage quota
A member cannot be added to the same team site twice

steps.label: IContentOrchestrator.RequestEditFileCheckpoint(cart, CMOperationType.AddFile) — quota + permission + parent folder check
PublishExecutor.PublishFile() — update Profile state + log Activity
Filter by TenantName and ActionType (ChangeRating, FileUpdated, ...)

gap_analysis.title: Anemic FileEntity — state transitions live outside the aggregate
gap_analysis.detail: FileManager.cs delegates entirely to FileRepository with no invariant-enforcing methods. Checkout/undo-checkout transitions (IsCheckedOut, CheckedOutBy), soft-delete guards, and permission enforcement are all mutated directly from FileWriter and the Orchestrator RequestEditFileCheckpoint lambda. entity.Checkout() and entity.UndoCheckout() methods do not exist; any caller that bypasses the orchestrator silently bypasses all invariants.

gap_analysis.title: All domain invariants encoded as Orchestrator Func factories, not aggregate preconditions
gap_analysis.detail: IContentOrchestrator.RequestEditFileCheckpoint() returns a Func<> that performs permission checks, quota validation, parent-folder existence, and content-state guards. This means the complete domain rule set is encoded as application-layer factory lambdas. Any Writer or background service that creates its own ScopedExpressContext can call the underlying repository directly without going through any invariant gate.

gap_analysis.title: PublishExecutor contains domain logic for publish-state transitions
gap_analysis.detail: PublishExecutor.PublishFile() updates Profile state, validates publishability, and writes audit records across multiple direct repository calls with no transactional aggregate boundary. These are domain operations that should be expressed as PublishMappingEntity.Publish(actorId, profileId, folderLocations). The entity does not exist; the concept is fully procedural.

gap_analysis.title: ExpirationJobExecutor owns the file-version expiration lifecycle
gap_analysis.detail: ExpirationJobExecutor.Run() directly queries expired versions, marks them expired, removes publish mappings, and logs activity — all imperative steps that belong inside FileVersionEntity.Expire(). The domain invariant that a version must be removed from all publish profiles before being marked expired is encoded only in the executor's execution order, invisible to anyone loading a FileVersionEntity.

gap_analysis.title: Controller couples directly to Writer classes without interface injection
gap_analysis.detail: FileController calls FileWriter.ReadLatestVersion() and FileWriter.AddFile() with no IFileWriter interface injected. The controller has a direct compile-time or runtime coupling to the concrete Writer class, making it impossible to unit-test the controller in isolation and violating the dependency-inversion principle throughout the Controller → Writer layer.

gap_analysis.title: Cart pattern couples domain query path to mutable HTTP-request-scoped state
gap_analysis.detail: Cart.Cart is a request-scoped cache created in every Writer and threaded through all Orchestrators. Domain repositories short-circuit to the Cart before hitting SQL. This couples the domain read path to a mutable object tied to a single HTTP request, making aggregate loading non-deterministic and Cart invalidation bugs silently serve stale state to callers in the same request.

gap_analysis.title: ActivityRepository.LogActivity called imperatively across 12+ layers
gap_analysis.detail: Audit logging is an afterthought side-effect performed by direct repository calls from Executors, Orchestrators, Writers, and background services. There is no DomainEvent mechanism; adding a new content operation requires remembering to call LogActivity in the correct place. Omitting it silently produces an incomplete audit trail with no compile-time guard.
gap_analysis.file: ActivityRepository.cs — called from ExpirationJobExecutor, PublishExecutor, SQLContentOrchestrator, FileWriter, and 8+ other classes

gap_analysis.title: No domain events raised from entities; Kafka publishing is ad-hoc imperative
gap_analysis.detail: ContentEvent is published to Kafka via direct calls to DiscEventV2Client from PublishExecutor and background services. No aggregate raises a domain event; there is no DomainEvent base class, no domain event dispatcher, and no EventSender abstraction in the domain layer. Downstream Kafka consumers have no formal contract tied to aggregate lifecycle state changes.

gap_analysis.title: 45+ bespoke exception classes instead of a DomainExceptionType enum pattern
gap_analysis.detail: The service has 45+ custom exception classes (FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, ContentDeleteException, CheckoutException, etc.) all extending ContentManagerException directly without a typed enum. ExceptionMiddleware maps class types to HTTP codes. Adding new exception semantics requires two changes (new class + new middleware mapping), and there is no single place to audit all domain error states.

gap_analysis.title: SQLDataRepository base exposes raw SqlDataReader to all repositories
gap_analysis.detail: SQLDataRepository.ExecuteSqlReader() returns a raw SqlDataReader iterated manually in every repository. This binds all domain repositories to SQL Server connection semantics, makes repositories impossible to test without a live database, and leaks infrastructure-specific exception types (SqlException) into domain call stacks.
gap_analysis.file: SQLDataRepository.cs — base class for FileRepository, FolderRepository, ProfileRepository, CustomPropertyRepository, and 10+ others

gap_analysis.title: DomainActionProvider polymorphism for content types lives in the Express layer
gap_analysis.detail: IDomainActionProvider / StandardDomainActionProvider / JourneyActionProvider / LessonActionProvider implement different behaviors per ObjectTypeId in an Express-layer DomainActionDispatcher. This content-type polymorphism belongs in the domain as a strategy on the ContentEntity aggregate, not as infrastructure-layer if/switch dispatch in the application orchestration module.

gap_analysis.title: 30+ Orchestrator interfaces fragment domain logic across the application layer
gap_analysis.detail: IContentOrchestrator, IFolderOrchestrator, IPermissionOrchestrator, IPublishOrchestrator, IUserOrchestrator, ITeamSiteOrchestrator, IProfileOrchestrator (30+ total) each hold fragments of domain logic. A single business operation such as AddFile requires creating and coordinating three Orchestrators — complexity that DDD resolves by having one aggregate enforce its own invariants with a single command method.

gap_analysis.title: Warehouse layer duplicates repository abstractions already defined in LibraryService
gap_analysis.detail: Express.Warehouse defines IFile, IFolder, IPermission, IProfile warehouse interfaces that duplicate IFileRepository, IFolderRepository, IContentPermissionRepository, IProfileRepository in LibraryService.Abstractions. Two parallel repository abstraction layers add indirection without adding isolation; changes to persistence contracts must be made in two places.

gap_analysis.title: LaunchDarkly feature-toggle concerns wired directly into controllers via filter attributes
gap_analysis.detail: Controllers use [DeprecatedByToggleFilter(FEATURE_STATEBASEDPUBLISHING)] attributes that invoke the LaunchDarkly SDK at the controller level. Feature flags are an infrastructure concern and should be resolved in an application service or middleware, not declared as routing attributes on controller actions.
